title: Communications
description: Review of wired interfaces, wireless links, cloud connectivity and USB: protocols, timeouts, robustness and certification settings.

items.text: Every protocol and message format is documented and versioned
items.hint: Including byte order, framing, checksums and the meaning of every field.

items.text: Receivers handle malformed, truncated and out-of-order messages
items.hint: Validate length and checksum before parsing. Fuzz the parser.

items.text: Timeouts and retries are defined for every request and response
items.hint: With a backoff, and a defined outcome when retries run out.

items.text: Debug and service ports are disabled or protected in production builds
items.hint: A console that accepts commands is an attack surface.

items.text: Link errors are counted and visible in diagnostics
items.hint: CRC errors, framing errors and timeouts per interface.

items.text: Regional radio settings (channels, power, duty cycle) match the certifications
items.hint: Firmware must not be able to exceed the certified configuration.

items.text: Test modes for radio certification are available, and locked out of production use
items.hint: Labs need continuous TX and fixed-channel modes. Document how to enter them.

items.text: Connection loss and reconnection are handled with backoff
items.hint: Thousands of devices reconnecting at once can overload the network or the backend.

items.text: The device works, or degrades gracefully, without connectivity
items.hint: Local control keeps working when Wi-Fi or the cloud is down.

items.text: Provisioning (joining a network) is tested with real phones and access points
items.hint: Include mixed-band networks, hidden SSIDs, captive portals and wrong passwords.

items.text: Coexistence between radios on the same device is managed
items.hint: E.g. Wi-Fi and BLE sharing a 2.4 GHz front end.

items.text: TLS is used with certificate validation, and a way to rotate root certificates
items.hint: Pin to a set of roots that can be updated by OTA, not a single leaf certificate.

items.text: The device-to-cloud API is versioned, so old firmware keeps working after backend changes
items.hint: Old firmware will be in the field for years.

items.text: Messages are queued or dropped by a defined policy while offline
items.hint: Bounded queue, with oldest-first or priority dropping.

items.text: Time is synchronized securely before it's used for certificates or schedules
items.hint: A device with no RTC battery boots in 1970, and certificate checks fail.

items.text: Telemetry volume and data costs are estimated per device per month
items.hint: Matters for cellular and for backend sizing.

items.text: USB descriptors use the client's own VID/PID, not the vendor's example IDs
items.hint: Example IDs collide with other products and aren't licensed for shipping.

items.text: Enumeration works on Windows, macOS and Linux hosts, and through hubs
Suspend, resume and cable unplug during transfers are handled
